A copy that fails because the running Wispr Flow process holds the file (the Windows share-lock case) names the cause and says to quit Wispr Flow and re-run\u0022,\u0022Every output lands under the node\\u0027s local voice directory \\u0060~/.hall9k/voice/\\u0060 (\\u0060%USERPROFILE%\\\\.hall9k\\\\voice\\\\\\u0060 on Windows) and nowhere else: never under a project home\\u0027s \\u0060repo/\\u0060, \\u0060tasks/\\u0060 or \\u0060ideas/\\u0060, never in the Postgres store, never in the message transport or the project ledger. On Unix the directory is created with owner-only permissions (0700)\u0022,\u0022The export reads the \\u0060History\\u0060 table ordered by \\u0060timestamp\\u0060 and writes \\u0060wispr-history-\\u003Cyyyy-MM-dd\\u003E-\\u003Cfull|lastNd\\u003E.json\\u0060 and \\u0060.csv\\u0060 with the columns and derived fields listed in the context below. \\u0060--days N\\u0060 restricts the window; a window that matches zero rows refuses to write empty files and says why\u0022,\u0022\\u0060h9k voice extract\\u0060 also writes \\u0060analysis/stats.md\\u0060, \\u0060analysis/edits.md\\u0060 and the five \\u0060analysis/chunk*.md\\u0060 sample files described in the context, using the same grouping, cleaning, selection and word budgets as the reference pipeline, with a seeded shuffle so two runs over the same export produce identical chunks\u0022,\u0022The command\\u0027s closing lines say how many rows were exported out of how many in the database, the local date range covered, and the directory written, and end with the one command that comes next (\\u0060h9k voice build-skill\\u0060, task B)\u0022,\u0022Unit tests cover the platform path resolution for both operating systems (a fixture, not the real home), timestamp parsing for the three formats the reference handled, the HTML cleaning rules, the destination mapping, and the chunk selection determinism. No test touches a real Wispr Flow database. The container-dependent integration tier is unchanged and still does not run on windows-latest\u0022,\u0022Decisions Log entry appended to PLAN.md \\u00A716 narrowing the \\u0022no voice\\u0022 non-goal: Hall9k still has no voice capture, and it does read the operator\\u0027s own Wispr Flow history, locally on that node only, as owner-scoped material for a generated skill. \\u0060docs/scope.md\\u0060 says the same in its own words. AGENTS.md\\u0027s command table gains the \\u0060h9k voice\\u0060 lines\u0022,\u0022\\u0060dotnet build\\u0060 and \\u0060dotnet test\\u0060 pass\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022## Why this exists\\n\\nBrian built a working version of this on his Mac as three TypeScript scripts (\\u0060export-wispr.ts\\u0060,\\n\\u0060voice-stats.ts\\u0060, \\u0060voice-sample.ts\\u0060) and used the output to author the \\u0060my-voice\\u0060 skill by hand.\\nThis task is the platform-native rewrite of the deterministic half of that pipeline, so that any\\nnode the owner runs can regenerate the material, and task B can turn it into a skill without a\\nhuman re-deriving it. The Mac scripts are not reachable from the Windows node, so everything the\\nimplementation needs is restated here.\\n\\n## Privacy boundary (binding, not advisory)\\n\\nThe Wispr Flow history is the operator\\u0027s own dictated speech: Slack messages, texts to family,\\nemail drafts, everything. The whole feature is bounded by one rule: **this data never leaves the\\nnode it was read on.** Concretely:\\n\\n- Output is node-local files under \\u0060~/.hall9k/voice/\\u0060. That directory is not a project home, not\\n  a repo, and not part of any render sweep. Nothing in this task writes a row to Postgres that\\n  contains dictation text; the store may record that an extract ran, when, and the row count, and\\n  nothing else.\\n- When the P2P layer\\u0027s owner-scope replication lands (IDEA-skill-layer, HALL9K-P2P-DESIGN.md), the\\n  voice directory and the generated skill (task B) are excluded from replication by default. Record\\n  that in the Decisions Log entry so the P2P work inherits the constraint rather than rediscovering it.\\n- The command refuses any \\u0060--out\\u0060 path that resolves inside a git working tree or a project home\\u0027s\\n  \\u0060repo/\\u0060. There is no flag to override this.\\n- Stats output (\\u0060stats.md\\u0060) may contain short n-grams and phrase counts. Chunk files contain\\n  verbatim dictations by design; they are the material task B reads and they stay in the same\\n  directory.\\n\\n## Platform detection\\n\\nWispr Flow is an Electron app; its user-data directory holds \\u0060flow.sqlite\\u0060 beside \\u0060Cache\\u0060,\\n\\u0060Code Cache\\u0060, \\u0060blob_storage\\u0060 and \\u0060config.json\\u0060.\\n\\n| OS | Data directory |\\n|---|---|\\n| macOS | \\u0060~/Library/Application Support/Wispr Flow/\\u0060 |\\n| Windows | \\u0060%APPDATA%\\\\Wispr Flow\\\\\\u0060 (Roaming) |\\n| Linux | \\u0060~/.config/Wispr Flow/\\u0060 (probe it, nothing more; no support claim) |\\n\\nResolve through \\u0060Environment.GetFolderPath\\u0060 (\\u0060ApplicationData\\u0060 on Windows, \\u0060UserProfile\\u0060 plus the\\nliteral \\u0060Library/Application Support\\u0060 on macOS) rather than string-building from \\u0060HOME\\u0060. The\\nWindows path is the one that must be verified on the node this task builds on; the macOS path is\\nverified in Brian\\u0027s own install and is the reference.\\n\\n## The History table\\n\\nColumns to read, in this order:\\n\\n\\u0060\\u0060\\u0060\\ntranscriptEntityId, timestamp, timezoneOffsetMinutes, app, url, platform, appVersion, status,\\nlanguage, detectedLanguage, asrText, formattedText, editedText, numWords, duration,\\nspeechDuration, conversationId, micDevice, hasRevertedAI, transcriptOrigin,\\nnumWordsCorrected, numDictionaryReplacements\\n\\u0060\\u0060\\u0060\\n\\nTimestamp handling: detect the format once from the first non-null value and apply it to every\\nrow. Three formats are known: epoch seconds (a number below 1e11), epoch milliseconds (a number\\nabove 1e11 or a 13-digit string), and an ISO-like string of the shape\\n\\u00602026-09-14 18:28:34.190 \\u002B00:00\\u0060 (space before the time and before the offset; normalise to\\n\\u00602026-09-14T18:28:34.190\\u002B00:00\\u0060 before parsing). The observed format on the reference database is\\nthe ISO-like string. Each exported row carries \\u0060timestampUtc\\u0060 (ISO 8601, \\u0060Z\\u0060) and \\u0060timestampLocal\\u0060\\n(\\u0060yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss\\u0060 in the node\\u0027s zone) in addition to the raw columns.\\n\\nRow selection for everything downstream of the raw export: \\u0060status == \\u0022formatted\\u0022\\u0060 and\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060 non-blank.\\n\\n## Text cleaning\\n\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060 and \\u0060editedText\\u0060 carry HTML fragments. Clean with, in order:\\n\\n1. \\u0060\\u003Cli\\u003E\\u0060 becomes newline plus \\u0060- \\u0060\\n2. opening or closing \\u0060ol\\u0060, \\u0060ul\\u0060, \\u0060p\\u0060, \\u0060br\\u0060, \\u0060div\\u0060 tags become a newline\\n3. any other tag is removed\\n4. \\u0060\\u0026nbsp;\\u0060 to space, \\u0060\\u0026amp;\\u0060 to \\u0060\\u0026\\u0060, \\u0060\\u0026lt;\\u0060 to \\u0060\\u003C\\u0060, \\u0060\\u0026gt;\\u0060 to \\u0060\\u003E\\u0060\\n5. trailing spaces before a newline removed, three or more newlines collapsed to two, then trim\\n\\nThe text used for analysis is the cleaned \\u0060editedText\\u0060 when it exists, differs from the cleaned\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060, and has at least 60 percent of its word count; otherwise the cleaned\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060. Word count is the number of non-whitespace runs.\\n\\n## Destination mapping\\n\\nFrom \\u0060app\\u0060 (case-insensitive regex) then \\u0060url\\u0060 host with a leading \\u0060www.\\u0060 stripped:\\n\\n| Match | Destination |\\n|---|---|\\n| \\u0060slack\\u0060 | \\u0060slack\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060MobileSMS\\u0060 | \\u0060imessage\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060Discord\\u0060 | \\u0060discord\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060whatsapp\\u0060 | \\u0060whatsapp\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060teams2\\u0060 | \\u0060teams\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060Outlook\\u0060 | \\u0060outlook\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060Terminal\\u0060 | \\u0060claude-code\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060claudefordesktop\\u0060 | \\u0060claude-desktop\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060parallels\\u0060 | \\u0060windows-vm\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060rdc\\u0060 | \\u0060remote-desktop\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060rowser\\u0060 or \\u0060zen\\u0060 (any browser) | \\u0060web:\\u003Chost\\u003E\\u0060 |\\n| anything else | the raw \\u0060app\\u0060 value, or \\u0060unknown\\u0060 |\\n\\nThe coarser grouping used by \\u0060stats.md\\u0060: \\u0060chat\\u0060 (slack, imessage, discord, whatsapp, teams),\\n\\u0060email\\u0060 (outlook, or web host containing outlook or teams), \\u0060claude-code\\u0060, \\u0060claude-desktop\\u0060\\n(including web host claude.ai), \\u0060jira-github\\u0060 (web host containing atlassian or github),\\n\\u0060windows\\u0060 (parallels, rdc), \\u0060browser-other\\u0060, \\u0060other\\u0060.\\n\\n## Statistics (\\u0060analysis/stats.md\\u0060, \\u0060analysis/edits.md\\u0060)\\n\\nComputed per group and for all rows together. No model is involved; this is arithmetic.\\n\\n- Counts: dictations, words, edited dictations.\\n- Length: sentence length median and p90 (split on \\u0060.\\u0060, \\u0060!\\u0060, \\u0060?\\u0060 followed by whitespace, or on\\n  newlines); dictation length median and p90 in words.\\n- Rates per 1,000 words: contractions (\\u0060\\u0027\\u0060 inside a word), question marks, exclamation marks,\\n  em dashes (U\\u002B2014), emoji (any codepoint in the emoji presentation ranges), semicolons,\\n  parentheses, colons, bullet lines. Also the share of dictations ending in \\u0060?\\u0060.\\n- Top hedges by rate: \\u0060just\\u0060, \\u0060I think\\u0060, \\u0060maybe\\u0060, \\u0060actually\\u0060, \\u0060kind of\\u0060, \\u0060probably\\u0060, \\u0060sort of\\u0060,\\n  \\u0060I believe\\u0060, \\u0060in my opinion\\u0060, \\u0060I could be wrong\\u0060.\\n- AI-tell watch list, reported even when zero: \\u0060moreover\\u0060, \\u0060furthermore\\u0060, \\u0060delve\\u0060,\\n  \\u0060great question\\u0060, \\u0060hope this helps\\u0060, \\u0060it\\u0027s worth noting\\u0060, \\u0060certainly\\u0060, \\u0060seamlessly\\u0060, \\u0060robust\\u0060,\\n  \\u0060additionally\\u0060, \\u0060circle back\\u0060.\\n- Top 25 openers and closers: the first and last three-word n-grams across dictations of eight or\\n  more words.\\n- Top 40 two-word and three-word n-grams overall.\\n\\n\\u0060edits.md\\u0060: for rows where the cleaned edit differs from the cleaned formatted text, a token-level\\nLCS diff, summarised as the top added tokens, top removed tokens, and 40 before/after pairs of\\nat most 60 words each.\\n\\n## Sample chunks (\\u0060analysis/chunk1..5\\u0060)\\n\\nShuffle with a linear congruential generator seeded from \\u0060--seed\\u0060 (default 20260914) so the\\nselection is reproducible: \\u0060seed = (seed * 1664525 \\u002B 1013904223) mod 2^32\\u0060. Fill each chunk in\\nshuffled order, skipping any row that would exceed the budget, stopping when the budget is met,\\nthen sort the chosen rows by local timestamp. Each entry renders as\\n\\u0060### \\u003CtimestampLocal\\u003E \\u00B7 \\u003Cdestination\\u003E \\u00B7 \\u003Cwords\\u003Ew\\u0060 followed by the text.\\n\\n| File | Filter | Budget |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| \\u0060chunk1-chat.md\\u0060 | destination in slack, imessage, discord, whatsapp, teams; 8\\u002B words | 11,000 words |\\n| \\u0060chunk2-human-web.md\\u0060 | outlook, or web host matching atlassian, github, outlook, teams, typeform, zendesk, dropbox, google.com, calendar; 8\\u002B words | 10,000 words |\\n| \\u0060chunk3-ai-short.md\\u0060 | claude-code, claude-desktop, windows-vm, remote-desktop, web:claude.ai; 6 to 49 words | 9,000 words |\\n| \\u0060chunk4-ai-long.md\\u0060 | same destinations; 120\\u002B words | 11,000 words |\\n| \\u0060chunk5-edits.md\\u0060 | edit exists, differs, row at most 120 words, edit at least 60 percent of formatted length | first 90 pairs after shuffle, rendered as \\u0060WISPR:\\u0060 / \\u0060SENT:\\u0060 lines |\\n\\n## Implementation notes\\n\\n- New \\u0060voice\\u0060 command group in \\u0060Hall9k.Cli\\u0060 on Spectre.Console.Cli, matching the existing\\n  command standards (worked example in \\u0060--help\\u0060, one bad invocation prints the command\\u0027s help).\\n- \\u0060Microsoft.Data.Sqlite\\u0060 added to \\u0060Directory.Packages.props\\u0060; it bundles the native SQLite\\n  library for both platforms. AGENTS.md\\u0027s command table gains the \\u0060h9k voice\\u0060 lines\u0022,\u0022\\u0060dotnet build\\u0060 and \\u0060dotnet test\\u0060 pass\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Why this exists\\n\\nBrian built a working version of this on his Mac as three TypeScript scripts (\\u0060export-wispr.ts\\u0060,\\n\\u0060voice-stats.ts\\u0060, \\u0060voice-sample.ts\\u0060) and used the output to author the \\u0060my-voice\\u0060 skill by hand.\\nThis task is the platform-native rewrite of the deterministic half of that pipeline, so that any\\nnode the owner runs can regenerate the material, and task B can turn it into a skill without a\\nhuman re-deriving it. The Mac scripts are not reachable from the Windows node, so everything the\\nimplementation needs is restated here.\\n\\n## Privacy boundary (binding, not advisory)\\n\\nThe Wispr Flow history is the operator\\u0027s own dictated speech: Slack messages, texts to family,\\nemail drafts, everything. The whole feature is bounded by one rule: **this data never leaves the\\nnode it was read on.** Concretely:\\n\\n- Output is node-local files under \\u0060~/.hall9k/voice/\\u0060. That directory is not a project home, not\\n  a repo, and not part of any render sweep. Nothing in this task writes a row to Postgres that\\n  contains dictation text; the store may record that an extract ran, when, and the row count, and\\n  nothing else.\\n- When the P2P layer\\u0027s owner-scope replication lands (IDEA-skill-layer, HALL9K-P2P-DESIGN.md), the\\n  voice directory and the generated skill (task B) are excluded from replication by default. Record\\n  that in the Decisions Log entry so the P2P work inherits the constraint rather than rediscovering it.\\n- The command refuses any \\u0060--out\\u0060 path that resolves inside a git working tree or a project home\\u0027s\\n  \\u0060repo/\\u0060. There is no flag to override this.\\n- Stats output (\\u0060stats.md\\u0060) may contain short n-grams and phrase counts. Chunk files contain\\n  verbatim dictations by design; they are the material task B reads and they stay in the same\\n  directory.\\n\\n## Platform detection\\n\\nWispr Flow is an Electron app; its user-data directory holds \\u0060flow.sqlite\\u0060 beside \\u0060Cache\\u0060,\\n\\u0060Code Cache\\u0060, \\u0060blob_storage\\u0060 and \\u0060config.json\\u0060.\\n\\n| OS | Data directory |\\n|---|---|\\n| macOS | \\u0060~/Library/Application Support/Wispr Flow/\\u0060 |\\n| Windows | \\u0060%APPDATA%\\\\Wispr Flow\\\\\\u0060 (Roaming) |\\n| Linux | \\u0060~/.config/Wispr Flow/\\u0060 (probe it, nothing more; no support claim) |\\n\\nResolve through \\u0060Environment.GetFolderPath\\u0060 (\\u0060ApplicationData\\u0060 on Windows, \\u0060UserProfile\\u0060 plus the\\nliteral \\u0060Library/Application Support\\u0060 on macOS) rather than string-building from \\u0060HOME\\u0060. The\\nWindows path is the one that must be verified on the node this task builds on; the macOS path is\\nverified in Brian\\u0027s own install and is the reference.\\n\\n## The History table\\n\\nColumns to read, in this order:\\n\\n\\u0060\\u0060\\u0060\\ntranscriptEntityId, timestamp, timezoneOffsetMinutes, app, url, platform, appVersion, status,\\nlanguage, detectedLanguage, asrText, formattedText, editedText, numWords, duration,\\nspeechDuration, conversationId, micDevice, hasRevertedAI, transcriptOrigin,\\nnumWordsCorrected, numDictionaryReplacements\\n\\u0060\\u0060\\u0060\\n\\nTimestamp handling: detect the format once from the first non-null value and apply it to every\\nrow. Three formats are known: epoch seconds (a number below 1e11), epoch milliseconds (a number\\nabove 1e11 or a 13-digit string), and an ISO-like string of the shape\\n\\u00602026-09-14 18:28:34.190 \\u002B00:00\\u0060 (space before the time and before the offset; normalise to\\n\\u00602026-09-14T18:28:34.190\\u002B00:00\\u0060 before parsing). The observed format on the reference database is\\nthe ISO-like string. Each exported row carries \\u0060timestampUtc\\u0060 (ISO 8601, \\u0060Z\\u0060) and \\u0060timestampLocal\\u0060\\n(\\u0060yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss\\u0060 in the node\\u0027s zone) in addition to the raw columns.\\n\\nRow selection for everything downstream of the raw export: \\u0060status == \\u0022formatted\\u0022\\u0060 and\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060 non-blank.\\n\\n## Text cleaning\\n\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060 and \\u0060editedText\\u0060 carry HTML fragments. Clean with, in order:\\n\\n1. \\u0060\\u003Cli\\u003E\\u0060 becomes newline plus \\u0060- \\u0060\\n2. opening or closing \\u0060ol\\u0060, \\u0060ul\\u0060, \\u0060p\\u0060, \\u0060br\\u0060, \\u0060div\\u0060 tags become a newline\\n3. any other tag is removed\\n4. \\u0060\\u0026nbsp;\\u0060 to space, \\u0060\\u0026amp;\\u0060 to \\u0060\\u0026\\u0060, \\u0060\\u0026lt;\\u0060 to \\u0060\\u003C\\u0060, \\u0060\\u0026gt;\\u0060 to \\u0060\\u003E\\u0060\\n5. trailing spaces before a newline removed, three or more newlines collapsed to two, then trim\\n\\nThe text used for analysis is the cleaned \\u0060editedText\\u0060 when it exists, differs from the cleaned\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060, and has at least 60 percent of its word count; otherwise the cleaned\\n\\u0060formattedText\\u0060. Word count is the number of non-whitespace runs.\\n\\n## Destination mapping\\n\\nFrom \\u0060app\\u0060 (case-insensitive regex) then \\u0060url\\u0060 host with a leading \\u0060www.\\u0060 stripped:\\n\\n| Match | Destination |\\n|---|---|\\n| \\u0060slack\\u0060 | \\u0060slack\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060MobileSMS\\u0060 | \\u0060imessage\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060Discord\\u0060 | \\u0060discord\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060whatsapp\\u0060 | \\u0060whatsapp\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060teams2\\u0060 | \\u0060teams\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060Outlook\\u0060 | \\u0060outlook\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060Terminal\\u0060 | \\u0060claude-code\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060claudefordesktop\\u0060 | \\u0060claude-desktop\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060parallels\\u0060 | \\u0060windows-vm\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060rdc\\u0060 | \\u0060remote-desktop\\u0060 |\\n| \\u0060rowser\\u0060 or \\u0060zen\\u0060 (any browser) | \\u0060web:\\u003Chost\\u003E\\u0060 |\\n| anything else | the raw \\u0060app\\u0060 value, or \\u0060unknown\\u0060 |\\n\\nThe coarser grouping used by \\u0060stats.md\\u0060: \\u0060chat\\u0060 (slack, imessage, discord, whatsapp, teams),\\n\\u0060email\\u0060 (outlook, or web host containing outlook or teams), \\u0060claude-code\\u0060, \\u0060claude-desktop\\u0060\\n(including web host claude.ai), \\u0060jira-github\\u0060 (web host containing atlassian or github),\\n\\u0060windows\\u0060 (parallels, rdc), \\u0060browser-other\\u0060, \\u0060other\\u0060.\\n\\n## Statistics (\\u0060analysis/stats.md\\u0060, \\u0060analysis/edits.md\\u0060)\\n\\nComputed per group and for all rows together. No model is involved; this is arithmetic.\\n\\n- Counts: dictations, words, edited dictations.\\n- Length: sentence length median and p90 (split on \\u0060.\\u0060, \\u0060!\\u0060, \\u0060?\\u0060 followed by whitespace, or on\\n  newlines); dictation length median and p90 in words.\\n- Rates per 1,000 words: contractions (\\u0060\\u0027\\u0060 inside a word), question marks, exclamation marks,\\n  em dashes (U\\u002B2014), emoji (any codepoint in the emoji presentation ranges), semicolons,\\n  parentheses, colons, bullet lines.
